title: Alphonso Davies to miss Canada’s March camp through injury, Jesse Marsch confirms
content:
After not playing for his country for nearly a year, Alphonso Davies will have to wait even longer to return to Canada’s men’s national team.

Davies suffered a hamstring strain for Bayern Munich on Tuesday during a 6-1 Champions League win over Atalanta, and Canada head coach Jesse Marsch confirmed on TSN 1050 radio Thursday that Davies will not join Canada in Toronto for friendlies against Iceland and Tunisia.

“(Davies) is probably not going to be with us for March, which is OK,” Marsch said.

After an ACL tear derailed much of Davies’ year in 2025, the 25-year-old had played eight Bundesliga matches before sustaining a torn muscle fiber on Feb. 21 against Eintracht Frankfurt. He then missed two Bundesliga matches.

While many inside Canada’s national team originally anticipated Davies returning to the national team later this month after the muscle fiber issue, his latest injury has derailed those plans.

“We’ll probably leave him there in Munich and make sure he gets himself fully fit and fully back to 100 percent,” Marsch said, “but I’m confident that he will do that.”

Davies last played for Canada on Mar. 23, 2025 during the Nations League Finals third-place game. During that game, Davies tore his ACL and spent the majority of 2025 recovering.

The injury led to a public war of words between Davies’ agent Nedal Huoseh, Bayern Munich executives and Canada Soccer over how the team handled Davies injury. In the aftermath, Canada Soccer showed they followed proper protocol handling the star left back after his injury.

Davies was named captain of Canada’s men’s national team not long after Marsch took over the Canada job in May 2024. Davies is expected to be one of the public faces of the team during the World Cup this summer, where Canada will co-host the tournament for the first time.

In Davies’ place, Canada is expected to lean heavily on Toronto FC left back Richie Laryea, who was arguably the best player for the national team through 2025. At left midfield, where Davies was also in contention to play, Norwich City midfielder Ali Ahmed will likely parlay his fine club form after a recent move to the English Championship into more starts for Canada.

Right now, Davies’ place in Canada’s World Cup squad is not in jeopardy. However a full year out of national team duty means Davies’ first games back will be immediately before the World Cup. Canada’s pre-World Cup friendlies are against Uzbekistan and Ireland in June.
